scope_note: US Ford passenger cars and light trucks 1928-1934: Model A (1928-31), 1932 Model B (four) and Model 18 (V8), 1933-34 Model 40 (four and V8). Model AA 1.5-ton truck noted only. HP = advertised brake hp (pre-SAE-gross era, treated as gross). cid rounded (200.5 -> 201). NHRA and EPA inputs empty (pre-NHRA/pre-EPA).

1932.name: 3.3L / 201 I4 L-head

sources.name: Ford 1932 Four-Cylinder Ford foldout (p.4 specifications)
sources.says: ENGINE 4-cylinder... Piston displacement, 200.5 cubic inches... Actual brake horsepower, 50 at 2800 r.p.m.; offered in fourteen standard or de luxe body types

1932.note: The four-cylinder '32 Ford. Same bodies as the V8 car; Ford's 1932 full-line brochure: 'An improved Ford four-cylinder, 50-horsepower engine, rubber mounted for smoothness... is available' for buyers who prefer a four. Counterweighted crankshaft added Nov 1932 (fordgarage).

1932.name: 3.6L / 221 V8 L-head

sources.name: Ford 1932 V-8 Features foldout (p.4 specifications) and V-8 foldout (p.4)
sources.says: ENGINE 8-cylinder, V-type, 90 degree... S.A.E. horsepower rating, 30; actual brake horsepower, 65; V-8 foldout: displacement 221 cubic inches

sources.name: Ford 1932 full-line brochure (pp.1, 2, 16)
sources.says: 8-cylinder, 65-horsepower, V-type engine... piston displacement is 221 cubic inches

sources.name: Hagerty Valuation Tools
sources.says: 1932 Model 18: 8-cyl. 221cid/65hp 1bbl

sources.name: Wikipedia - 1932 Ford (Model B / Model 18 / Model 40) and Ford flathead V8 engine
sources.says: 221 cu in V8 rated 65 hp; 5.5:1 compression

sources.name: EngineLabs - Historic Engines: The Fabulous Ford Flathead
sources.says: 221 ci, 65 hp at 3,400 rpm

sources.name: Mac's Motor City Garage - Henry's Other '32 Ford: The Four-Cylinder Model B
sources.says: 65 hp and 130 lb-ft for the V8

1932.note: The V8 '32 Ford (the hot-rod 'Deuce'). In 1932 the Model 18 is the V8 car and the Model B the four-cylinder car, same bodies. V8 introduced spring 1932; 3-1/16 x 3-3/4 bore/stroke; single-barrel downdraft carburetor. Ford material (two brochures) counted as one source.

1933.note: Availability confirmed by 4 sources; the 50 hp figure is explicit only in Hagerty and implied by Wikipedia ('unchanged'). No Ford 1933 literature found online that rates the four (US 1933 brochures cover the V8 only). 'Model C' is a collector nickname (C head casting / counterweighted crank), not a Ford designation.

1933.name: 3.6L / 221 V8 L-head

sources.name: Ford 1933 V-8 Salesman booklet (pp.4-5, 12) and 1933 Ford foldout (side A)
sources.says: The engine now develops 75 horsepower at 3800 revolutions per minute, an increase of 10 horsepower over that of the former V-8 engine; aluminum cylinder heads, higher compression; 221 cu. in. Foldout: 'V-type eight-cylinder engine; 75-horsepower. All-aluminum cylinder heads'

sources.name: Wikipedia - 1932 Ford (Model B / Model 18 / Model 40) and Ford flathead V8 engine
sources.says: rose to 75 hp; 6.33:1 compression

sources.name: EngineLabs - Historic Engines: The Fabulous Ford Flathead
sources.says: aluminum heads raised the horsepower rating to 75 for the Model 40

sources.name: Hagerty Valuation Tools
sources.says: 1933 Model 40: 8-cyl. 221cid/65hp 1bbl (DISAGREES)

1933.note: Ford's 1933 salesman booklet gives 75 hp at 3800 rpm (+10 over 1932); Wikipedia and EngineLabs agree. Hagerty lists 65 hp, the 1932 figure, apparently carried over in error. 112-in wheelbase from 1933.

1934.note: Last year of the Ford four (dropped for 1935); very low volume. 50 hp stated by Hagerty and conceptcarz only; no Ford 1934 literature found rating it (1934 US brochures cover the V8 only).

1934.name: 3.6L / 221 V8 L-head

sources.name: Ford 1934 V-8 foldout (p.5), 1934 Ford foldout (p.6), 1934 full-line brochure (p.16)
sources.says: V-type eight-cylinder engine. Greater horsepower, more speed... new dual down-draft carburetor and dual intake manifold; 221 cubic inches (no hp figure printed)

sources.name: Wikipedia - 1932 Ford (Model B / Model 18 / Model 40) and Ford flathead V8 engine
sources.says: horsepower 'increased, this time to 85 hp' for 1934 (Wikipedia's flathead-engine article instead lists 75 hp for 1933-34)

sources.name: EngineLabs - Historic Engines: The Fabulous Ford Flathead
sources.says: two-barrel Stromberg carburetor raising output to 85 horsepower in the Model 40A

sources.name: conceptcarz - Ford Model 40 (Dan Vaughan articles)
sources.says: 85 horsepower at 3,800 RPM; up 10 over 1933

sources.name: Hagerty Valuation Tools
sources.says: 1934 Model 40: 8-cyl. 221cid/90hp 2bbl (DISAGREES)

1934.note: 85 hp per Wikipedia (1932 Ford/Model 40 text), EngineLabs and conceptcarz; Ford's 1934 brochures confirm only 'greater horsepower' than 1933's 75 from the new dual downdraft (Stromberg) carburetor and manifold. Dissent: Hagerty 90 hp; Wikipedia flathead article 75 hp for 1933-34. No 1934 Ford document printing the number was found online. [2026-10-15: rating withheld; sources give 75, 85 and 90 hp and no 1934 Ford figure was found.]
